summary: Deep green nephrite jade polished to a soft, waxy lustre, glowing a little where light gets in, as in carvings and beads.
_comment: Polished nephrite jade: a felted mass of fine amphibole fibres, polished to a soft, waxy lustre; a deep, saturated green, cloudy rather than banded, with paler and deeper green clouds, a faint fibrous streak and the odd black speck. SUBSURFACE: jade's look is light getting into it, a few millimetres, green travelling furthest. subsurface_color is ONE constant, the texture's mean linear albedo (the library cannot drive a textured article's scatter colour from its texture), so at subsurface_weight 0.75 the clouds keep about 25 % of their contrast, and the generator draws them strongly for it. Redone 2026-10-22 on the maintainer's note (reads sage: a deeper, more saturated jade green, more translucency): the colour anchor went from (0.055, 0.14, 0.065) to (0.020, 0.135, 0.036), the weight from 0.6 to 0.75 (0.85 flattened the clouds away) and the radius from 4 to 6 mm. Base textures are generated (L2, tools/converters/base/gen_nephritejade_polished.py), as the wish list plans: ambientCG has no jade asset. Carries every relevant wear layer at 0 (C1): scratches (overlay 1, damage), dust as a deposit (Phase10), water spots, gated by the Crevice mask. Built by the Phase11 batch.
name: NephriteJade_Polished_Clean_Base_s01_v01

sources.why: Mean linear albedo (0.020, 0.135, 0.036), about sRGB 39, 103, 53, for a deep, saturated nephrite green (the first anchor, sRGB 66, 105, 72, read sage); roughness about 0.14 for jade's waxy polish; specular_ior 1.61 (nephrite about 1.60-1.63); subsurface_weight 0.75, subsurface_color the mean albedo, subsurface_radius 0.006 m with green travelling furthest (0.45, 1.0, 0.55): good nephrite is translucent several millimetres in. Physically Based has no jade entry.
